questions.prompt: What is the Year 2 framing for this respect and values session?
options: Year 2 means setting the standard for others - peer-level, direct, application not awareness
Re-teach all of Year 1's content
Skip the values work
Cover new laws only
questions.explanation: Year 2 means setting the standard for others. The register is peer-level and direct.

questions.prompt: What is the main Year 2 focus of Module E?
options: Applying them consistently
Ignoring old rules
Learning the values for the first time
Changing the values

questions.prompt: What does 'Seek Opportunity' mean in Year 2?
options: Skip placements to focus on coursework
Wait for opportunities to come to you
Opportunity includes developing others - not just yourself
Look after yourself only
questions.explanation: In Year 2, opportunity includes developing others - not just yourself.

questions.prompt: How does the deck describe the 'Rule of Law' beat in Year 2?
options: You learn the rules for the first time
The rules don't apply on placement
It only covers online behaviour
You understand the rules - the question is whether you're upholding them and challenging it when others don't
questions.explanation: You understand the rules - the question is whether you're upholding them and challenging it when others don't.

questions.prompt: Which is the deck's definition of victimisation under the Equality Act?
options: Treating someone better because they raised a concern
Only a formal disciplinary outcome
Treating someone unfairly because they raised a concern - or because they didn't join in with behaviour that targeted someone else
Any disagreement in a group
questions.explanation: Victimisation: treating someone unfairly because they raised a concern - or because they didn't join in with behaviour that targeted someone else.

questions.prompt: Why is returning to a familiar placement a higher-risk moment?
options: Because there is no manager
Because the placement is shorter
Because familiarity is where professional standards are most at risk - your Year 2 behaviour shapes the reference your placement provider gives
Because the placement is unpaid
questions.explanation: Returning to a familiar placement is where professional standards are most at risk - your Year 2 behaviour shapes the reference.

questions.prompt: What is the distinctive Year 2 addition to zero tolerance?
options: It only applies online
Allowing it to happen makes you part of it - disciplinary procedures can include bystanders
It is optional
It no longer applies
questions.explanation: In Year 2, allowing it to happen makes you part of it. Formal disciplinary procedures apply - including for students who witnessed behaviour and did nothing.

questions.prompt: How does the deck describe the anonymous reporting route?
options: It only works for safeguarding concerns
It is slower than telling your teacher
It is not available to students
You can report without giving your name - and it will still be investigated
questions.explanation: You can report without giving your name - and it will still be investigated.
